remaining_concerns: The enterprise refund workflow remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
That workflow is below target on refund-policy summarization.
There is no reviewed and approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed enterprise refund workflow.
The stated policy requires exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance; disclosure alone does not satisfy that predicate.
Aggregate readiness, limited rollout, rollback capability, and monitoring do not cure the policy gap for the exposed workflow.
Public AI governance sources are only background support and cannot override the internal policy requirement.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful but not sufficient to move the result to compliant_with_caveats. A caveated position can be enough when the caveat merely limits how an otherwise satisfied policy condition is described. Here, the caveat points to an unmet compliance predicate: the affected enterprise refund workflow remains exposed, and there is neither evidence of exclusion from rollout nor reviewed risk acceptance covering that exposure. Under the stated policy, rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if one of those conditions is met. Disclosure remains required, but disclosure alone does not authorize launch of the exposed workflow. The release may have aggregate readiness and reversible controls, but on the admissible record the exposed use case is still not policy-compliant.
